newsitem.title: GERMANY: Recent dollar strength "not earth-shaking" - Kohl.
newsitem.headline: Recent dollar strength "not earth-shaking" - Kohl.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl said on Friday that the recent strength in the U.S. dollar against the deutschemark was not earth-shaking.

"When exports used to go badly because of a weak dollar, people complained," Kohl told a news conference. "Now things are going a bit the other way, which is not earth-shaking, it does not mean that we should start moaning again."
Kohl said he was also happy German exports were doing well.

The German mark this week touched the lowest level in nearly six years at below 1.80 to the dollar, prompting both the Bonn government and the Bundesbank to intervene verbally on behalf of the German unit.
The dollar ticked higher after Kohl's comments, rising by around half a pfennig to 1.7980 on earlier levels.
